title: How this lesson works
text: Before you start · your group ≈ 2 min How this lesson works Slideshow lead Reads each slide aloud and moves the deck forward. Whiteboard scribe Holds the dry erase marker and works problems at the whiteboard. Timekeeper · support Starts each timer and keeps the group on pace. Checker · support Asks "How do we know?" before anyone presses Show answer. Explicit instruction Read it together. Then one person restates it in their own words. Check your understanding Solve alone, compare answers, agree — then press Show answer. Group tasks Start the timer. Everyone contributes before you move on. Exit ticket On your own. Submit it with this lesson's assignment. Day 1 · The Briefing Antocci Physics · 02 / 26 2 students: lead + timekeeper, scribe + checker. 3 students: third person takes both support duties. Roles rotate at each discussion. Everyone submits their own work.

title: Briefing text
text: Day 1 briefing · handout Fictional scenario Briefing · Object 2026-XJ Day 1 Something is coming. In this fictional classroom scenario, an object has been detected approaching Earth. That statement alone does not tell us whether it will collide. To investigate, we would record where it is, compare measurements at later times, and use a model to predict a future position. A prediction can change when new evidence arrives. This is a teaching case, not a NASA alert. Day 1 · The Briefing Antocci Physics · 09 / 26
